summary.title: How do some people get stuck at a senior engineer position while a few rise up to EVP level in big organizations like Microsoft, Amazon, Apple, Google?
summary.one_liner: Senior engineers who want to move past the senior level must expand scope, influence people without authority, build relationships and sponsors, and learn to get work done through others, not just write better code.
keywords: how to get promoted to principal engineer
what got you here won't get you there
takeaways: Promotions are based on expected future value at the higher level, not past work; advancing requires expanding scope from features to products and org processes.
Influence without authority, stakeholder management, and building relationships with managers and peers are key to moving above senior.
Senior IC is reached through technical strength, but higher levels require identifying work yourself and getting results through others.
Staying an engineer is a valid choice; the page argues that management or cross-functional skills are the usual route upward, and warns against forcing top engineers into management.
summary.summary: This is a Quora Q&A thread where several answerers, including one who went through Microsoft's Bench program, explain why many engineers plateau at senior level. The top answer argues that promotion depends on expanding scope and cross-team impact, and that communication, socializing, and hard work matter as much as engineering skill. Other answers note that the path upward usually runs through managing people and cross-functional skills, and that big companies have a ceiling for pure engineers. The page also includes a long, generic AI-style checklist on the executive path (scope ladder, sponsorship, roadmap by year) that is not attributed to a named author.
